task.title: Two branches into main: fast-forward and conflict
task.description:
You are in the ~/portfolio folder on the main branch. There are two branches: feature/footer adds footer.html (main has not changed since it was created), and feature/title changes the heading in index.html - the same line that was also changed in main after the split. Write the commands one per line: 1) Look at the history of all branches as a graph. 2) Merge feature/footer into main - it must be a fast-forward (without --no-ff). 3) Merge feature/title - there will be a conflict in index.html. 4) Look at git status and the content of index.html. 5) Resolve the conflict by combining both versions: write index.html with the command cat > index.html << 'EOF' - the first line is

Anna Karimova, web developer - Portfolio

, the second line is

Junior web developer

, with no conflict markers. 6) Mark the conflict as resolved and finish the merge with a commit (git commit without -m takes the ready message Merge branch 'feature/title'; you can also use -m). 7) Delete both merged branches with the safe command git branch -d. 8) Look at the history graph and make sure that the working directory is clean.
task.starter_code:
# Write commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments. # You are in the ~/portfolio folder on the main branch. There are branches feature/footer and feature/title. # 1. Look at the history of all branches as a graph # 2. Merge feature/footer into main (it will be a fast-forward) # 3. Merge feature/title - there will be a conflict in index.html # 4. Look at git status and the content of index.html # 5. Write the final index.html with cat > index.html << 'EOF' # line 1:

Anna Karimova, web developer - Portfolio

# line 2:

Junior web developer

# 6. Mark the conflict as resolved (git add) and finish the merge with a commit # 7. Delete both merged branches with git branch -d # 8. Look at the history graph and git status
task.setup:
sim.user.config["user.name"] = "Anna Karimova"; sim.user.config["user.email"] = "anna@example.com"; sim.user.config["init.defaultBranch"] = "main"; sim.run(`mkdir portfolio && cd portfolio && git init echo "

Anna Karimova

" > index.html echo "

Junior web developer

" >> index.html git add . && git commit -m "Add home page" mkdir css && echo "body { margin: 0; }" > css/style.css git add . && git commit -m "Add styles" git switch -c feature/title echo "

Anna Karimova - Portfolio

" > index.html echo "

Junior web developer

" >> index.html git commit -am "Add portfolio to title" git switch main echo "

Anna Karimova, web developer

" > index.html echo "

Junior web developer

" >> index.html git commit -am "Add profession to title" git switch -c feature/footer echo "
2026 Anna Karimova
" > footer.html git add footer.html && git commit -m "Add footer" git switch main `, { quiet: true });

hints: You merge into the current branch: make sure you are on main and run git merge feature/footer. The output should say Fast-forward.
After git merge feature/title, Git writes CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in index.html. This is not an error but a question to you.
cat index.html shows the markers: between <<<<<<< HEAD and ======= is the main version, between ======= and >>>>>>> feature/title is the branch version.

questions.question: You are on the main branch and ran git merge feature/menu. What happens?
options: The changes from main are moved into feature/menu
The changes from feature/menu are moved into the current branch, main
The branches swap places
A new branch with both versions is created
questions.explanation: git merge always merges the given branch into the current one. The feature/menu branch does not change.

questions.question:
What did Git print?

$ git merge feature/footer
Updating 549439a..6d00d19
Fast-forward
 footer.html | 1 +
options: A merge commit with two parents was created
The main pointer was simply moved forward to the branch commit - no new commit was created
A conflict happened
The feature/footer branch was deleted
questions.explanation: Fast-forward: main has not changed since the split, so Git simply moves its pointer to the latest commit of the branch.

questions.question: When does git merge create a merge commit (Merge branch ...)?
options: If both branches got new commits after the split
If the --no-ff option is given
If the branch is ahead of main, main has not changed, and there are no options
If the branch has only one commit
questions.explanation: A merge commit is needed when the histories have split, or when it is asked for explicitly with --no-ff. Otherwise Git does a fast-forward.

questions.question: Match the conflict marker with its meaning.
pairs: The start of the current branch's version
The border between the two versions
The end of the merged branch's version
questions.explanation: Between <<<<<<< and ======= is your version (HEAD), between ======= and >>>>>>> is the version from the branch you are merging.

questions.question:
Why did the conflict happen?

CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in index.html
options: There is an HTML error in index.html
After the split, both branches changed the same lines of index.html in different ways
The index.html file was deleted in one of the branches
The branches were created by different people
questions.explanation: Git merges changes in different places of a file by itself. A conflict happens only when one place was changed in both branches and Git does not know which version is right.

questions.question: What do you need to do to finish a merge with a conflict?
options: Edit the file: keep the needed text and remove all the markers
git add the file - mark the conflict as resolved
git commit - create the merge commit
git branch -D the branch that caused the conflict
questions.explanation: The order: fix the file → git add → git commit. You do not need to delete the branch for this - it is deleted with -d after a successful merge.

questions.question: Type the whole command: cancel a merge that caused a conflict and put everything back as it was before git merge.
questions.explanation: git merge --abort returns the working directory and the index to the state before the merge. The branch itself does not go anywhere - you can merge it later.

questions.question:
What does this git status output mean?

All conflicts fixed but you are still merging.
  (use "git commit" to conclude merge)
options: The merge is completely finished
The conflicts are marked as resolved with git add; you still need to run git commit
You need to run git merge again
The merge is cancelled
questions.explanation: "All conflicts are fixed, but you are still in the middle of a merge" - Git is waiting for git commit, which will create the merge commit.

questions.question: You ran git add index.html without removing the <<<<<<< markers, and then git commit. What happens?
options: Git refuses: there are markers in the file
The commit is created, and the markers get into the website - the browser shows them as text
Git removes the markers by itself
The merge is cancelled
questions.explanation: Git does not check the content of the file: git add means "I have fixed everything". So before git add, always open the file and check that there are no markers.

questions.question: Match the VS Code button above a conflict with the result.
pairs: Keep the version of the current branch (HEAD)
Keep the version of the merged branch
Keep both versions, one under the other
Show the two versions side by side
questions.explanation: Current is the current branch, Incoming is the incoming (merged) branch. Both keeps both versions, and usually you still need to fix them by hand.

questions.question: The feature/footer branch is already merged into main. Type the whole command: safely delete this branch.
questions.explanation: -d deletes only a merged branch: if it has unmerged commits, Git refuses (error: the branch ... is not fully merged).
